transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

To be honest, I get stuck in front of the mirror or looking at photos of myself, trying to fix how I look, and it’s starting to mess with my work and my runs. It’s pretty embarrassing to admit at my age, but it's gotten to the point where I just can't seem to shake it.
When you look in the mirror or at photos, do you find yourself focusing on one or more specific parts of your body that you believe look flawed or ugly, even if other people say they look normal?

Yes, it's my face—I can't stop focusing on how bent my nose looks, my jaw being off, and my skin looking like old leather. I'll spend hours zooming in on photos of myself and constantly ask my sister and kids if I look lopsided. It's incredibly stressful because to me, it just looks completely wrong.
Do you believe these appearance concerns could be exaggerated by your mind, or are you completely convinced that your nose, jaw, or skin really are abnormal or deformed?

I am completely convinced it’s real and not just in my head. To me, my nose looks undeniably bent, my jaw is totally off, and my skin looks like old leather. That is why I'm constantly asking my family for reassurance, because I genuinely see myself as lopsided and deformed.
Have you ever wondered whether these appearance problems might not actually be real, or are you completely certain that your nose, jaw, or skin is truly deformed?
I'm not really sure, I haven't really thought about it that way. When I look in the mirror, it just looks so real to me that it's hard to imagine it being any other way.
Have you ever had a doctor or other clinician examine your nose, jaw, or skin and tell you that there is no actual deformity or abnormality?
No, I haven't actually seen a doctor or any kind of specialist to examine my face or skin. I've mostly just been worrying about it on my own and asking my sister and kids if they notice it.
Have you ever felt that other people might not see these facial problems the way you do, or do you believe others are hiding the truth and can clearly see the deformity too?

I'm not really sure what other people truly see or if they are just hiding the truth to spare my feelings. Because it feels so incredibly obvious to me, though, I constantly ask my family for reassurance to see if they notice it too.
Do you ever believe that other people are talking about your appearance, laughing at you, or deliberately hiding the truth about how deformed your face looks?

I don't think people are necessarily laughing at me or lying to my face about it. It's more that I just feel incredibly self-conscious and scrutinized whenever others look at me, like they are noticing all my flaws.
Have you ever been completely certain that other people are talking about your appearance, mocking you, or deliberately hiding the truth about how deformed your face looks?

No, I've never been completely certain of that, and I don't have any proof that people are actively mocking me or hiding things. I just feel incredibly self-conscious all the time and constantly worry that they are judging how I look.
Do these concerns make you do repetitive behaviors like checking mirrors or photos, comparing your appearance to others, or seeking reassurance, and about how much time do you spend on them each day?

Yes, I lose hours every day stuck in front of the bathroom mirror or zooming in on photos on my phone—tilting my head, picking at my skin, shaving repeatedly, and changing shirts over and over. I also constantly ask my sister and kids if I look lopsided, and these routines take up so much time that I end up showing up late or skipping work and my runs entirely.
Have you ever become completely certain that other people are mocking you, talking about your appearance, or deliberately hiding the truth about your face being deformed?

No, I don't think people are deliberately mocking me or lying to me about my appearance. It's just that I feel incredibly self-conscious, and I feel like they are judging my weathered, crooked face when they look at me.
Do you ever become completely convinced that your face is truly deformed, even when others disagree, or do you recognize that these worries might be excessive or not fully accurate?

In the moment, it feels completely real and convincing to me, and I'm certain my face looks wrong. But when my family tells me they don't see it, I do sometimes wonder why they don't see what seems so obvious to me. I'm just not entirely sure what to think.
Have you ever been completely certain, without any doubt, that other people are talking about your appearance, mocking you, or deliberately hiding the truth about your face being deformed?

No, I've never been completely certain of that, and I don't think people are actively mocking me or hiding some secret. I just feel incredibly self-conscious and constantly worry about how I look to them, which is why I keep asking my family for reassurance.

When you notice these appearance concerns, do you ever hear or see things that other people do not, or feel completely certain that someone is watching, mocking, or trying to harm you because of how you look?

No, I’ve never seen or heard things that aren't there, and I don't think anyone is out to get me or trying to harm me. I just feel extremely self-conscious and constantly worry about how people are judging my appearance. It's more about my own anxiety than feeling like there is some conspiracy against me.
Do you think there is any chance that your concerns about your face could be a misperception or be exaggerated, or are you completely certain they are true despite what others tell you?

To me, these flaws feel completely real and undeniable, and my face looks obviously crooked and lopsided whenever I look in the mirror. I honestly struggle to believe how anyone could look at me and not notice it right away. Even though my sister and kids try to reassure me, I feel like they are just trying to be nice to spare my feelings, leaving me convinced that what I see is the absolute truth.
Have you ever been able to recognize that these appearance concerns might be excessive or possibly not true, even briefly, or are you completely certain your face is deformed all the time?
I'm not really sure if I've ever truly doubted it. When I look in the mirror or at photos, my face genuinely looks so crooked and deformed to me that it's hard to think any other way.
Have you ever been able to consider that your appearance concerns might be exaggerated or possibly not true, even briefly, or are you completely certain all the time that your face is deformed?

It's hard to say because the flaws feel completely real and obvious to me, so I haven't really thought about whether it's exaggerated. When I look at myself, what I see just feels like the absolute truth.
When you are not looking in the mirror or at photos, do you still believe with complete certainty that your face is deformed, or can you acknowledge there is a chance you may be misperceiving it?

Even when I'm not looking, the worry is always there and it feels incredibly real and distressing to me. I honestly don't know how to answer whether it's a misperception or if I'm absolutely certain, but it just constantly weighs on me.
When you are away from mirrors or photos, can you acknowledge that there is a chance your face may not actually be deformed, or are you completely certain it is deformed all the time?

It’s really hard to say, and I’m not completely sure how to answer that. Even when I'm not looking in a mirror, I just can't shake the feeling that something is terribly wrong with my face. It always feels so real to me in the moment, so it's tough to know if there's a chance I'm just misperceiving it.
Do you ever think there is even a small chance that your face may not actually be deformed, or are you absolutely certain it is deformed no matter what anyone says?

When I look at myself, it feels completely real and undeniable—my face looks genuinely battered, crooked, and lopsided to me. Even though I constantly ask my sister and kids for reassurance, their answers never really change how convinced I am when I look in the mirror or at photos. It just feels like the absolute truth, no matter what anyone says.
Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that people are trying to harm you, spy on you, or control you, even when there was no clear evidence for it?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've never felt like people were trying to harm me, spy on me, or control what I do. My worries have always just been about my own appearance and how I look to others.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder: persistent preoccupation with perceived facial defects (nose, jaw, skin), repetitive checking/camouflaging/reassurance-seeking behaviors, marked distress and functional impairment, and poor insight with near-delusional conviction about the appearance flaw. No hallucinations, broader delusions, or primary psychotic symptoms were elicited.
